reason: The text prominently emphasizes hierarchy through multiple structural elements: David is portrayed as supreme authority commanding Joab and military commanders; the narrative explicitly states the king's word prevails over Joab's objections (וּדְבַר־הַמֶּלֶךְ חָזַק עַל־ יוֹאָב); subordinates demonstrate ritual deference (Arnan bows prostrate before David - וַיִּשְׁתַּחוּ לְדָוִיד אַפַּים אָֽרְצָה); and there is a clear chain of command from God to David to Joab to the people. The narrative structure reinforces David's position at the apex of earthly authority, with obedience flowing downward through the hierarchy.
